Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick follow-up to capture the sizing inputs we discussed and confirm a fallback/ladder strategy for bursts. We want to make sure any Dedicated pool we propose meets your steady-state needs while letting you absorb spikes without hitting outages or excessive cost.

Ask: can you confirm the following (or attach the workload snapshot you mentioned)?
- Baseline sustained TPS target (requests/sec)
- Typical token-per-request (prompt + gen), plus distribution (e.g., % <200 tokens)
- Expected peak/spike TPS and typical duration (minutes / hours)
- Whether you rely on prefix/KV caching for session context or mainly stateless calls
- Any hard latency SLOs (p50/p95) we should honor for the POC

We can then propose: a baseline H100 pool sized for steady throughput, an autoscale ladder to add more H100s for mid-size bursts, and an L4-based read-only offload tier for high-volume short prompts (if quantization looks good). If you prefer to avoid heterogeneous pools we can propose a uniform H100-only autoscale plan.

I've attached the export you referenced (opsense-workload-snapshot.csv) to make this concrete. Once you confirm numbers I’ll run a quick capacity estimate and share a recommended ladder + cost delta.

Next steps I propose:
1) You send the confirmed numbers or update the snapshot by EOD tomorrow
2) We deliver a 1–2 page recommended capacity ladder + cost estimate the following day
3) If that looks good, we schedule a short call to lock POC dates

Thanks —

Thanks for the clear notes. I pulled the numbers from our telemetry and pasted the key pieces below; the team also uploaded a fuller export to the shared Drive.

Summary:
- Baseline sustained TPS: 120 req/s (steady business hours)
- Typical token-per-request: mean 400 tokens (prompt ~80 tokens, gen ~320 tokens)
- Token distribution: ~80% of requests are short queries (<200 tokens), ~15% medium (200–800), ~5% long (>800)
- Peak/spike: intermittent hourly spikes to ~2,500 req/s lasting 5–15 minutes (user churn during batch ingestion windows); daily peak window ~SLO aware
- Concurrency: many parallel user sessions; average concurrency per model shard ~32 active streams
- Cache usage: we use KV caching for sessions (~35% of calls hit cached prefixes), but many batch inference jobs are stateless
- Latency SLO: p95 generation <= 800ms for short queries; for long generations we can accept up to 3s during spikes

Procurement note: we’d like to run a 2-week POC in October and evaluate both Dedicated and Private VPC options (security team will confirm whether Private is required before production).

Let me know if you need any more detail.

Jonas —

Good data from Opsense. A few quick internal clarifying questions before we finalize the ladder:

- When Maya says "KV caching ~35% hit", do they cache prefix keys for generation or full KV for chat sessions? That changes memory profile.
- For the long tail (~5% >800 tokens), is that mostly batch/ETL inference we could schedule on off-peak nodes, or is it user-facing interactive generation?
- For the 2,500 req/s spikes: Are those primarily short prompts? If so, we can offload to quantized L4s as a cost effective burst strategy.

Initial sizing thought (preliminary):
- Baseline: 4 x H100-80GB as primary pool (steady-state 120 TPS with room for typical concurrency and cache)
- Mid-burst ladder: add +8 H100s to handle up to ~800–1,200 sustained TPS (longer bursts)
- Burst-offload: spin up up to 32 x L4 (quantized 8-bit) to handle short prompt floods (target up to 2,500 req/s for short queries)
- Autoscale policy: scale ratio favoring H100 for medium-length gen and L4 for short queries; route by token-length heuristics and model-compatibility

Risks & notes:
- KV cache: if Opsense keeps large KV state per session, memory-bound H100 counts may rise — need exact per-session KV footprint (MB/session)
- Latency SLO: mixing L4 for short queries should hit p95 < 800ms but must validate in POC with the same network topology (especially if Private VPC)
- Cost: L4s lower cost per token but may require model quantization work — ask if they accept 4-bit/8-bit behavior in POC

I attached a quick estimate workbook (dedicated-sizing-estimate-v1.xlsx) — drop in KV sizes and average generation length and it recalculates pool sizes and cost deltas.

If that looks reasonable, Jonas — want me to draft the recommended ladder + cost delta and slot a call with Opsense for Thursday?

Thanks,
Ben

Maya —

Thanks for the telemetry and Ben for the rapid sizing. Based on what Opsense shared, here is our recommended Dedicated pool ladder and next steps (high level):

Recommended configuration (POC):
- Baseline pool: 4 x H100-80GB (handles steady 120 TPS with room for concurrency and ~35% KV hit)
- Mid-burst scale: autoscale to +8 H100 (total 12 H100) for medium-length gens (200–800 tokens)
- Short-prompt burst-offload: up to 32 x L4 (quantized 8-bit) that can be spun up for the 5–15 minute spike windows; route short requests (<200 tokens) to L4s
- Model variants: production uses compiled H100 kernels; we’ll supply a quantized L4 variant for short prompt routing during spikes
- Fallback policy: if H100 capacity exhausted, route non-latency-critical jobs to queued H100 slots or to L4 if compatible; provide graceful degradation to lower token cap rather than returning errors

Security & deployment options:
- We can run the same ladder in a Private VPC (customer-managed networking) if your security team requires it — POC can be in Redwood Dedicated with a VPC-simulated network topology, then migrate to Private in production if requested.

Costs & timeline (estimate):
- Baseline 4x H100: estimate $X/day (I'll attach a detailed PDF with ranges).
- Adding mid-burst H100s increases cost linearly; L4 offload reduces cost-per-short-query during spikes significantly.
- Proposed POC: 2 weeks, starting the week of Oct 11. We’ll validate p95 latency targets and scale behavior with your exact traffic pattern.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-proposal.pdf (2-page proposal and estimate)

Next steps (please confirm):
1) Opsense approves the POC plan + capacity ladder (thumbs up)
2) Redwood creates a POC configuration and shares ingress keys + small test harness (1 business day)
3) Joint runbook: Opsense runs 2 sample spike windows while we observe and tune autoscale rules

Would Thursday (Oct 1) 11am PT work for a 30-min sync to walk the proposal and lock dates?

Regards,
